scope: Synthetic native PostgreSQL 16 / MinIO handler measurements; no production data

method.transport: Fiber httptest to real handlers, native database and real indexed object data; synthetic identity injection

actor_roles.member: Current database membership with settings and chats permissions
actor_roles.admin: Current database account administrator; private ACL predicates remain enabled

method.quantiles: nearest rank; p95 equals maximum with ten samples
method.seeding: Real object writes and native SQL rows in batches of 1000; all production triggers enabled; timing also includes fixture validation
method.indexing: Explicit production reconciler drained after fixture creation, without the background worker 2-second inter-cycle wait; measured separately from seed and HTTP samples; ANALYZE outside samples; not an end-to-end background freshness SLA
method.shared_shape: One physical object, 10000 authorized message uses in 101 real Chats; no text-only messages
method.memory_scope: Go test process only; PostgreSQL and MinIO excluded; baseline after explicit GC and FreeOSMemory
method.allocation_scope: Cumulative Go allocations during request batch; not retained or resident memory
method.gc_scope: Go collections and pauses observed during the timed request batches only
method.s3_assertion: A real S3 proxy counter must remain unchanged during all timed samples and the extra memory batch; no mocked S3 responses
method.parallelism: Page-open scenarios issue files and usage concurrently; remaining samples are sequential; no sustained multi-user load
limitations: Synthetic Chat media data only; no production storage investigation or numbers
No claim of end-to-end browser or authenticated network latency
No constant-latency claim: exact counts, summaries, substring search and large offsets retain data-dependent SQL work
Admin is measured against the same Chat dataset; this does not represent large private Work/Pizarras hierarchies or grants
Uniform 1 KiB objects, one reference per object in main cohorts; no large JSON or recovery-heavy workload
Shared /uses detail still materializes authorized uses before slicing the HTTP page; measured separately
SQL rows of preceding cohorts remain until database teardown; object prefixes are cleaned after their cohort
Two warmups do not establish cold-start performance; database plan/cache choices can vary within the ten samples
10 ms Go RSS/heap sampling may miss short peaks; database and object-store process memory is not measured
Historical comparison is between different implementations and separate runs, not a contemporaneous controlled A/B experiment
